correctness.rationale: The proof correctly starts from the published admissibility criterion. For p=2, even f factors 2^f-1 into coprime nontrivial factors and modulo-three divisibility eliminates all but f=2,4; for odd composite f the proper divisor 2^a+1 and the 3-power analysis eliminate admissibility. For odd p, even f≠2 over p=3 creates incompatible 4- and 3-divisibility, while p=3 reduces to f=2. For odd composite f, the factor (p^a+1)/2 is already composite and Bang–Zsigmondy supplies an outside prime, excluding both prime-power and squarefree-semiprime forms. At odd prime f, primitive divisors force p>3 to have both consecutive integers (p-1)/2,(p+1)/2 prime, hence p=5; p=3 and 5 then reduce to the stated exact factors. An independent comparison of the source criterion and reduced criterion for all primes p≤19 and 2≤f≤12 found zero mismatches. The cited Zsigmondy applications avoid the classical exceptions.
